linguistics.meaning: Deliverance — 'the saving / rescuing of people', the abstract noun of paspîhiwêw 's/he saves people'.
linguistics.type: NI noun (deverbal abstract / nominalization of a VAI verb)

morphemes.gloss: Verbal initial: escape, get free of, slip out of. The same initial sits inside paspiw 's/he escapes (gets through alive)' and paspâpiw 's/he peeks out (through a hole)'.
Causative connector: 'cause / make'. Turns an intransitive escape‑event into an action done to someone.
VAI indefinite‑object final: '(to) people'. Used when the object of the action is generic / human (rescue people, save folks, teach people).

Abstract noun deriver: turns the verb paspîhiwêw 's/he saves people' into the noun paspîhiwêwin 'a saving / rescue / deliverance'. The same ‑win is in pimâtisiwin 'life' (from pimâtisiw 's/he lives').

relatedForms.english: S/he saves people, s/he rescues people (the underlying VAI verb)

morphemes.gloss: VAI indefinite‑object 3sg suffix: 's/he (does it to) people'.

relatedForms.note: Strip ‑win off the plaque headword and you are back to the verb 's/he saves people'. The plaque chose the abstract noun for the trail name; the verb itself is what a rider does on the rescue ride out.

relatedForms.english: S/he escapes, s/he gets through (alive) — the bare VAI base

morphemes.gloss: VAI base: get through, escape (the short‑i variant of the initial).

relatedForms.note: Bare‑intransitive escape verb — the first‑person rider's reading. Where paspîhiwêwin is the abstract act of rescuing others, paspiw is what the survivor does themselves.

relatedForms.english: S/he saves him/her (animate object, VTA sibling)

morphemes.gloss: VTA 3→3′ indicative suffix: 's/he does it to him/her (animate)'.

relatedForms.note: VTA sister of the plaque verb: switches the indefinite ‑iwê‑ 'people' for a definite animate object. Use this when you want to say 's/he saved her', not 's/he saves people'.

quickReference.note: Plaque headword. itwêwina/CW gloss: 'rescue, saving people, deliverance / vindication'.

quickReference.english: S/he saves people, s/he rescues people
quickReference.note: VAI 3sg — the verb whose nominalization is on the plaque.
Same paspî‑ initial + ‑âpi‑ 'look / peek' final. Shows the productivity of the paspî‑ 'slip through' initial.
Built from pimâtisiw 's/he lives' + ‑win 'abstract noun'. Same machinery as the plaque headword.

baseWords.english: (initial) escape, get through, slip out of

culturalStory.heading: Through Patricia Ravine
body: In MTB vernacular a trail earns the name Deliverance by where it puts you and by what it asks of you to get out. On the wall, Deliverance sits paired with Purgatory — the same flame‑palette pivots into a wider banjo‑and‑bridge medallion, a winding pool of blue water threading underneath the bridge's pilings. The banjo is the John Boorman Deliverance reference (the 1972 film, the duelling‑banjos river); the bridge under it is the engineering of getting out alive. Black field, silver bridge, blue water, red Cree syllabics floating across the bridge deck — the design reads as a single rescue tableau.

The Cree carved onto the plaque, paspîhiwêwin, is the abstract noun of paspîhiwêw 's/he saves people' (itwêwina/Wolvengrey). The Plains Cree dictionary glosses it simply: rescue, saving people, deliverance, vindication. The same root paspî‑ 'slip through, escape, get out alive' is what makes paspiw 's/he survives' and paspâpiw 's/he peeks out through a hole' — the morpheme that runs through the whole family is the idea of getting through a narrow opening. That is also the literal shape of the trail: Patricia Ravine Upper, the black‑diamond singletrack threading through the steep, narrow ravine on Edmonton's west side.

Geographically the trail is the official 'Deliverance' on Trailforks (id 13244, Patricia Ravine Upper, 902 m, black diamond) — paired on the ground with 'Bed Springs' (Patricia Ravine Lower) and on the wall with 'Purgatory'. The whole sequence sits on ᓀᐦᐃᔭᐤ ᐊᐢᑭᕀ Nêhiyaw‑Askiy (Plains Cree territory) on the south rim of the North Saskatchewan, and is part of an Edmonton‑area effort to put Plains Cree names back onto the trails this network's riders have known by their English nicknames for a long time.

notes: CATALOGUE CORRECTION PROPOSED: catalogue.json currently has creeName = 'deliverance' (placeholder) and creeSyllabics = '' for this sign. The plaque is carved with SRO 'paspîhiwewin' (long‑î on pî) and syllabics ᐸᐢᐲᐦᐃᐍᐏᐣ. Propose catalogue update to creeName = 'paspîhiwêwin' (adding the ê circumflex to match syllabics and itwêwina), creeSyllabics = 'ᐸᐢᐲᐦᐃᐍᐏᐣ'. The plaque carved‑SRO drops the ê circumflex on 'we' (same pattern as the Purgatory plaque); the syllabics ᐍ (we, long‑ê by definition) implies the circumflex. itwêwina/Wolvengrey headword is 'paspîhiwêwin' with both diacritics.

Trailforks: high‑confidence match — 'Deliverance' / 'Patricia Ravine (Upper)' trail id 13244 in the Edmonton region. Trailhead 53.50799, ‑113.59977 (FAQ, Whitemud Park parking 1.8 mi, Terwillegar Park parking 2.0 mi). Pairs with 'Bed Springs' = Patricia Ravine Lower. ~95% confidence.

Image asset: docs/assets/deliverance/sign_render.png is a tight wall crop from allSigns.jpg (box ≈ (5380, 2950, 6300, 4300) in 8160×6144 original), re‑encoded as a real PNG. The folder had no root design image — the banjo‑and‑bridge DALL·E source in the sibling purgatory/ folder appears to be the original Deliverance graphic that got filed under the wrong folder. The wall crop is the authoritative photo.

Morpheme bracketing: paspî‑ + ‑h‑ + ‑iwê‑ + ‑win is one defensible split (the one used in this page). An alternative collapses ‑hiwê‑ into a single 'cause‑people' VAI final and treats ‑h‑ as part of that final rather than a separate causative connector. Either is teachably correct.

The paspî‑ initial is the same one that gives paspiw 's/he escapes (alive)' and paspâpiw 's/he peeks out'. The reduction paspî‑ → paspi‑ in paspiw is the standard initial‑vowel shortening before a bare VAI ‑w; flagged for completeness.
